title: User API errors during morning peak
executive_summary: INC-009 (SEV2) caused elevated errors on user endpoints (GET /v1/users/{id}) affecting api-gateway and user-service, starting around 08:00Z on 2026-09-26. Final status is ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED with a leading hypothesis of a deployment regression, with confidence 0.68. The most probable explanation is that the user-service 7.2.0 release (ORM batch-loader switch, dep-c02e51b7), which completed at 07:56Z, introduced an application-level NullPointerException in ProfileBatchLoader.load. The first such error (logpat-user-service-2347725d) appeared at 07:57:17Z. user-service error rate rose from about 0.4% to about 23% and p95 latency rose from about 80 ms to about 670 ms (met-user-service-error_rate-0730-0825, met-user-service-p95_latency_ms-0730-0825). api-gateway forwarded these 500s to clients, with its error rate rising from about 0.5% to about 8% and the first gateway WARN at 08:00:08Z (logpat-api-gateway-c1d874f7). Database connection utilisation, CPU, and request rate stayed flat, which fits an exception-path fault rather than resource saturation. The postgres report_rollup slow-query hypothesis (H2) and the untracked-trigger hypothesis (H3) were both rejected.

hypotheses.description: The user-service 7.2.0 release (ORM batch-loader switch, dep-c02e51b7) introduced an application-level fault in ProfileBatchLoader.load that fails a subset of GET /v1/users/{id} requests with 500s, which api-gateway surfaces to clients. Mechanism: Deploy 7.1.3->7.2.0 completes at 07:56Z -> ProfileBatchLoader.load throws NullPointerException on affected requests from 07:57:17Z -> user-service error_rate steps from ~0.4% to ~23% and p95 rises ~80->~670 ms (retries/slow failing paths) -> api-gateway forwards user-service 500s (error_rate 0.5% -> ~8%, first gateway WARN 08:00:08Z) -> users see errors on user endpoints. DB connection utilisation, CPU, request rate and timeouts stay flat, consistent with an exception-path fault rather than resource saturation.

critic_review.summary: H1 (user-service 7.2.0 application fault in ProfileBatchLoader.load) is supported by independent sources that agree on timing. The deploy completed at 07:56Z. The first NPE (tagged v7.2.0) is at 07:57:17Z, and no earlier NPE appears in the 07:30-08:30 query. The user-service error_rate steps from about 0.41% (07:55 sample) to 22.8% (08:00 sample) and p95 steps from about 72-86 ms to about 670 ms. Gateway 500s for user-service start at 08:00:08Z. Metrics for postgres (p95, connections), user-service DB connections, CPU/request rate, and p99 stay flat, which fits an exception-path fault rather than resource saturation. Caveats: the log query was PARTIAL, so the "no NPE before 07:57" claim rests on the records returned, not on complete coverage. There is no per-version or per-endpoint breakdown and no rollback/canary check yet. These are limitations, not blockers. The order-service flatness is unexplained but is consistent with a path-specific fault. H2 is rejected: postgres p95 and connection utilisation are flat, and the step at 07:57 is about 21 minutes after the first slow report_rollup, with no matching change in the error pattern. H3 is rejected: the config-change query for 07:00-08:30 returned no changes, and the NPE is explicitly tagged to v7.2.0. Feature flags are not visible to the tools, so that gap is noted.

assessments.reasoning: Deploy at 07:56Z, NPE tagged v7.2.0 from 07:57:17Z with no earlier occurrences in the returned data, and a metric step at 07:57 (error_rate 0.41 to 22.8, p95 80 to 670 ms) that matches. Gateway 500s follow at 08:00:08Z. Resource metrics are flat, consistent with an application fault. Limitation: logs are partial; a rollback or per-version breakdown would strengthen this further.

Postgres p95 (~12 ms) and connection utilisation are flat across the window, and user-service DB connection utilisation is flat too. The first slow report_rollup (07:36Z) precedes the abrupt error step at 07:57 by about 21 minutes with no intervening change. No evidence links report_rollup to user-service tables.

Config-change query for 07:00-08:30 returned no changes. The NPE is explicitly tagged to v7.2.0 in ProfileBatchLoader, so the deploy is the better-supported cause. The only support is a flat order-service metric, which H1 also has to explain. Untracked feature flags remain possible but have no positive evidence.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): deployment_regression in user-service - The user-service 7.2.0 release (ORM batch-loader switch, dep-c02e51b7) introduced an application-level fault in ProfileBatchLoader.load that fails a subset of GET /v1/users/{id} requests with 500s, which api-gateway surfaces to clients.
corrective_actions: Roll back user-service from 7.2.0 to 7.1.3 (the last known-good release) to restore user endpoint availability, then confirm error_rate returns to baseline (~0.4%).
Verify the rollback by checking that the NullPointerException in ProfileBatchLoader.load (logpat-user-service-2347725d) stops appearing in logs after the rollback time.
Confirm rollback scope: check that all user-service instances are running 7.1.3, since no per-version breakdown has been checked yet.
Check api-gateway retry and timeout behaviour during the incident and reduce client-facing 500s if the gateway amplifies failures.
preventive_actions: Fix the null-handling defect in ProfileBatchLoader.load introduced by the batch-loader switch, and add a unit or integration test covering the failing path before re-releasing 7.2.0.
Gate future releases of user-service with a canary or staged rollout and automated error-rate/p95 comparison against the baseline, so a regression like this is halted before full rollout.
Add a pre-deploy check for ORM or data-access changes that exercises GET /v1/users/{id} with representative data, including profiles that may produce null batch results.
Investigate why order-service error rate stayed flat during the incident, to understand whether the failing path is endpoint-specific and whether similar batch-loader code exists elsewhere.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on user-service error_rate exceeding a threshold above the ~0.4% baseline (for example, >2% over 5 minutes), and on p95 latency above ~200 ms.

conclusion: The most probable root cause of INC-009 is the user-service 7.2.0 deployment, which introduced a NullPointerException in ProfileBatchLoader.load. This caused user-facing 500s on GET /v1/users/{id}, which api-gateway surfaced to clients. The timing across the deploy, the first error, the metric step changes, and the gateway errors all agree, and resource metrics stayed flat. This is the most probable explanation, not a fully confirmed one: the log query was partial, no per-version or per-endpoint breakdown was checked, and no rollback or canary test has yet been run. Rolling back to 7.1.3 and confirming recovery is the priority action. The postgres report_rollup and untracked-trigger hypotheses were rejected on timing and evidence.
